modeRationale: No Nintendo platform has a native achievement/trophy system (confirmed for Switch/Switch 2). FireRed/LeafGreen have never shipped on a platform with native achievements (GBA cartridge only, no Steam/PS/Xbox release). No native list exists anywhere to port from.

platformVerification.summary: Pokémon FireRed and Pokémon LeafGreen released digitally as two separate SKUs on both Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 on February 27, 2026 (Pokémon Day, 30th anniversary), $19.99 each, digital-only, no physical release. Confirmed via Nintendo's own 'What's New' page plus GameInformer, TechRadar, Nintendo Life, 9to5toys. NOT part of the Nintendo Switch Online GBA app/subscription library — a deliberate standalone release per Nintendo (Nintendo Life interview).
platformVerification.confidence: high (Nintendo's own announcement page cited by 2 of 3 scouts)
platformVerification.contentChanges: Reported as otherwise content-identical to the 2004 GBA original. Confirmed genuine changes: (1) GBA Link Cable/Wireless Adapter trading & link battles replaced by Switch local wireless, LOCAL-ONLY — no online multiplayer/trading at all, even on Switch 2; (2) Mystic Ticket and Aurora Ticket (Navel Rock/Ho-Oh+Lugia, Birth Island/Deoxys) are now auto-granted after the first Champion win, instead of requiring historical real-world event distribution. Mew's Old Sea Map event was NOT added — Mew remains unobtainable. No new story content, areas, or difficulty options reported.
platformVerification.confidenceNote: All Switch-specific mechanical claims rest on secondary gaming press (Serebii, VGC, NintendoLife, TechRadar, GameRant, PokeCommunity), not an official Nintendo patch-notes document. Treat as medium confidence.

gymLeaders.name: Giovanni
gymLeaders.note: Also the Team Rocket boss; final Team Rocket confrontation.

campaign.champion: The rival, 'Blue' by default English name (anime: Gary). Team is starter-counter themed incl. Pidgeot, Alakazam, Rhydon, levels ~58-63 (exact roster not independently cross-verified against one authoritative source — low-medium confidence on exact composition).
campaign.rivalBattles: 8 encounters: Pallet Town (mandatory), Route 22 pre-Viridian-Forest (optional), Cerulean City (mandatory), SS Anne (mandatory per most sources; one claims skippable via a traded Cut-Pokémon — unverified, do not rely on this), Pokémon Tower (mandatory), Silph Co. (mandatory), Route 22 rematch before League (mandatory), Pokémon League/Champion (mandatory, final). No in-game rival-battle counter exists.
teamRocketStoryline: Mt. Moon — first appearance, fossil theft, weak grunts. Mandatory.
Rocket Hideout under Celadon Game Corner — first Giovanni fight, yields Silph Scope. Mandatory.
Pokémon Tower, Lavender Town — rescue Mr. Fuji, yields Poké Flute. Mandatory.
Silph Co., Saffron City — building takeover, second Giovanni fight, yields Master Ball. Mandatory.
Viridian City Gym — Giovanni as final Gym Leader AND final main-story Team Rocket boss; he quits after this loss. Mandatory (8th badge).
campaign.cinnabarMansion: LOW CONFIDENCE / UNCONFIRMED: one scout could not confirm whether Cinnabar Island Mansion has an active Team Rocket combat encounter in FRLG, or is purely exploratory/lore (burned Mewtwo research notes). Treat as optional exploration/lore content, not a combat story beat, unless re-verified.
campaign.seviiIslandsRocketReturns: FireRed/LeafGreen-exclusive post-League subplot (absent from original Red/Blue/Yellow): Rocket hideout on One Island (Mt. Ember, searching for the Ruby), kidnapping/rescue of Lostelle in Berry Forest (Three Island), climax at a Rocket Warehouse in Five Isle Meadow (Five Island) recovering the Sapphire from Admins/a Scientist. The antagonist's name ('Gideon') appeared in only one low-quality source — DO NOT use this name in any trophy text.

mewtwo.unlock: Beat Elite Four + obtain National Pokédex (60+ species registered) + complete Sevii Islands Ruby/Sapphire quest to repair Celio's Network Machine, which physically opens the Route 4 cave entrance.
mewtwo.CONFLICT: Scouts disagree on whether delivering only the Sapphire, or both Ruby AND Sapphire, is required to unlock the cave. One source says Sapphire only; another/synthesized source says both gems. UNRESOLVED — do not hard-code a specific gem requirement into trophy text; phrase verification around 'completing the Sevii Islands Network Machine questline' instead.

campaign.ending: Single ending only: defeating the Champion triggers Hall of Fame registration + credits (no branching). Hall of Fame is a persistent record screen of registered teams; unclear if it increments per repeat clear (gap).

collectiblesAndSideContent.kantoDex: 151 numbered slots, but Mew (#151) is not obtainable through any normal/legitimate method on this release (no Old Sea Map / Faraway Island event added for Switch). 150/150 is the realistic completion target. A cosmetic Kanto Dex Diploma is viewable at Celadon Mansion for catching 150 — purely cosmetic, no gameplay effect.
collectiblesAndSideContent.nationalDex: 386 species total, unlocked after registering 60 Kanto species + beating the Elite Four. CONFIRMED IMPOSSIBLE to complete on this Switch release: ~166 species historically required trading from Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald/GameCube-era games, and this release has no online trading or bridge to those games (no Pokémon HOME integration confirmed at launch). Do NOT design a National Dex completion trophy.

seviiIslands.overview: 9-island archipelago exclusive to FireRed/LeafGreen (absent from original Red/Blue): One through Seven Island, plus event-locked Navel Rock and Birth Island. Reached via Seagallop Ferry after Blaine (6th gym) + meeting Bill/Celio.
seviiIslands.gating: Tri-Pass (One-Three Island) available early. Rainbow Pass (Four-Seven Island) requires Elite Four + National Dex + retrieving the Ruby from Mt. Ember.
seviiIslands.content: Team Rocket Returns subplot (see campaign). Berry Forest (Three Island) — maze with regenerating wild berries (Oran, Persim, Pinap, Aspear, Bluk, Wepear, Cheri), also where Lostelle is rescued. Trainer Tower (near Seven Island) — post-game battle facility, 4 modes (Single/Double/Mixed/Knockout), each first clear gives a unique evolution item (Up-Grade/Dragon Scale/King's Rock/Metal Coat per one source, mode-mapping not independently cross-confirmed). English release has no e-Reader support (Japan-only feature), fixed 4 floors — a claim that Switch bumped this to 8 floors is single-source and unverified, treat as false until confirmed.

collectiblesAndSideContent.safariZone: Fuchsia City. Catch-only (Bait/Rock mechanic, no battling). Notable rarities: Chansey, Kangaskhan, Tauros, Dratini (fishing), and version-exclusive Scyther (FireRed)/Pinsir (LeafGreen) — also independently purchasable at the Game Corner. The sole source of a Lucky Egg is a wild Safari Zone Chansey holding one (community-estimated low odds, not officially quantified — avoid hard-coding a percentage in any trophy).
collectiblesAndSideContent.gameCorner: Celadon City. Only minigame: slot machines (gambling for Coins, exchanged for prizes). No Voltorb Flip (that's a HeartGold/SoulSilver feature, confirmed absent here). Coins are directly purchasable with Pokédollars, so a coin/purchase-threshold trophy avoids relying on slot RNG. Version-exclusive prize Pokémon: Scyther (FireRed, 5500 coins) vs Pinsir (LeafGreen, 2500 coins) — independently corroborates the wild-encounter version split.
collectiblesAndSideContent.bugCatchingContest: CONFIRMED ABSENT. This is a Johto (Gold/Silver/Crystal/HGSS) National Park feature — FireRed/LeafGreen has no National Park and no Bug-Catching Contest. Do not reference it.
collectiblesAndSideContent.dodrioBerryPicking: Minigame at the Two Island Joyful Game Corner. Historically required the GBA Wireless Adapter + 3-5 linked players each with a Dodrio — i.e. genuinely multiplayer-dependent, not solo-playable even on original hardware. On Switch this would map to local wireless with other physical consoles present.
collectiblesAndSideContent.moveTutors: 15 total across Kanto + Sevii Islands, each teaches one move once per save for free (Mega Punch, Mega Kick, Seismic Toss, Rock Slide, Counter, Softboiled, Mimic, Thunder Wave, Substitute, Dream Eater, Metronome, Double-Edge, Explosion, Body Slam, Swords Dance).
collectiblesAndSideContent.fanClub: Vermilion City Fan Club Chairman gives a Bike Voucher (free Bicycle from the Cerulean Bike Shop) after a one-time dialogue.
collectiblesAndSideContent.dlc: None exists or ever existed for this game, on any platform, confirmed by both historical record and the 2026 rerelease being a complete standalone package.

trackableStats: Badge Case / Trainer Card front — 8 badges, play time, trainer ID (money-on-card unconfirmed)
Pokédex Seen/Owned counters — Kanto regional dex and National dex, viewable any time in the Pokédex menu; Oak also gives milestone rating dialogue

Trainer Card back — Hall of Fame Debut date, Link Battles count, Pokémon Trades count, Union Trades/Battles, Battle Points, Berry Crush participation (several of these reflect legacy GBA Wireless Adapter / Pokémon Emerald-shared features; behavior on Switch's local-wireless reimplementation not independently confirmed)

Trainer Stars (medium confidence, single source family) — awarded for: first Champion win; 200 Pokémon Jump + 200 Dodrio Berry Picking; Kanto Dex complete (minus Mew); National Dex complete (minus Mythicals). Exact total star count (4 vs 5) unconfirmed.

versionExclusivePokemon.fireRed: Ekans, Oddish, Psyduck, Growlithe, Shellder, Scyther families (medium confidence; some aggregator lists fold in evolutions/baby forms not independently 'exclusive' as wild encounters — re-verify exact base-species list before finalizing trophy wording)
versionExclusivePokemon.leafGreen: Sandshrew, Vulpix, Bellsprout, Slowpoke, Staryu, Magmar, Pinsir families (same caveat as above)
versionExclusivePokemon.corroboration: Independently confirmed via Game Corner prize differences: Scyther=FireRed, Pinsir=LeafGreen.

missables: Starter choice (Bulbasaur/Charmander/Squirtle) — the other two require trading with a second physical console; this release has no online trading, so a solo player locks them out permanently.
Fossil choice at Mt. Moon (Helix→Omanyte vs Dome→Kabuto) — picking one forecloses the other for that save.
Gift Lapras (Silph Co., Lv.25, after the rival battle there) — one-time.
Two single-encounter wild Snorlax (Route 12 and Route 16) — if fainted without catching, gone for that save (medium confidence on exact non-respawn rule for this remake specifically).

9 fixed one-time in-game NPC trades (Mr. Mime for Abra, Nidoran-M/F swap, Nidorino/Nidorina swap, Lickitung for Golduck, Jynx for Poliwhirl, Farfetch'd for Spearow, Seel for Ponyta, Electrode for Raichu, Tangela for Venonat) — several (Mr. Mime, Jynx, Farfetch'd, Lickitung) are otherwise very hard/impossible to get any other way, making them de facto required stops for Pokédex completion. Exact route numbers have minor source disagreement on 1-2 entries.
progressionStatsAndMissables.multiplayerDependentContent: Trade-evolutions (Kadabra→Alakazam, Machoke→Machamp, Graveler→Golem, Haunter→Gengar), the two non-chosen starters, and Dodrio Berry Picking all require a second physical Switch/Switch 2 console with a second copy of the game and a second player, over LOCAL WIRELESS ONLY (no online trading/battling exists on this release at all, even on Switch 2). Per Rule 13, no trophy should require these.

rng.shinyOdds: 1/8192, no Shiny Charm or odds-boost exists in this generation — too rare for a fair trophy.
rng.criticalCapture: Does not exist in Generation III mechanics (introduced Gen IV) — do not design around this.
rng.gameCornerSlots: RNG-based, but coins are directly purchasable with money, so a coin-threshold trophy is not meaningfully RNG-gated.
rng.safariZoneRares: Layered RNG (catch factor + flee chance + base rarity) for species like Chansey/Kangaskhan/Dratini/Tauros; exact encounter rates not quantified by research — flagged as a possible excessive-RNG risk if a trophy demands one specific rare species rather than 'a' Safari Zone catch.
